methods.label: Combine the logarithms
methods.explanation:
Use the standard convention that the logarithms are real and share one fixed base \(b>0\), \(b\ne1\). Their arguments require \(p>0\) and \(q>0\).

The product rule combines the left side, giving
\[
\log(pq)=\log(p+q).
\]
Equal logarithms with the same base have equal arguments, so
\[
pq=p+q,\qquad p(q-1)=q.
\]
The case \(q=1\) would give \(0=1\), so it is impossible. Also, \(q-1=q/p>0\), which shows \(q>1\). We may therefore divide to obtain
\[
p=\frac q{q-1}.
\]
Conversely, any \(q>1\) with this value of \(p\) gives positive arguments and satisfies \(pq=p+q\), so it satisfies the original logarithmic equality. Thus the required relation is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\), with \(q>1\) and \(p>1\).
